title: Reference evaluation
description: One append-only craft-evidence record about a reference (AES-V2.3 / SUE-561). A reference is evaluation context, never a template, and it may never establish a fact — see docs/architecture/V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md §2 and editorial/RIGHTS-AND-PROVENANCE.md for the pointer/rights layer this record sits beside. Records are never overwritten; a later opinion is a new record with `supersedes` set.

ref_id.description: Must resolve to an entry in references/catalog.json and matches the pattern used by schemas/editorial-intent.schema.json's reference_input.

modality.description: Which evaluate-reference profile under editorial/profiles/reference/ this record was produced against.

calibration_ref.description: The calibration snapshot active when this evaluation was made (AES-V2.10). Null when no calibration has been activated yet.

profile_ref.description: Repository path of the reference-evaluation profile used.

basis.description: explicit_human_feedback: the human said it. model_inference: an agent judged it. Load-bearing — agent consensus may never silently stand in for human preference.

dimensions.description: Per-dimension craft verdicts. Dimension ids come from the matching modality profile's `dimensions[].id`.

authority_boundary.description: This record grants craft evidence only, never factual authority. A reference may never establish a fact.

provenance_class.description: Where this reference actually came from. Load-bearing against self-reinforcement: as this system generates more, its own outputs become the most plentiful and most semantically relevant references, so selection that ignores origin quietly converges on its own tics.

promotion.description: Present only when a generated_output reference has been promoted to a reusable positive reference (i.e. carries an adopt verdict). Publication is not promotion and an L1 pass is not promotion — see references/REFERENCE-EVALUATION-PROTOCOL.md. Absent on every unpromoted record.

authorized_by.description: Who or what authorized the promotion, e.g. "human:owner".

basis.description: Why this counts as promotion evidence. "published" or "L1 pass" alone is insufficient and is rejected by scripts/registry.mjs.

evidence_refs.description: Ids of the feedback/evaluation records or explicit owner declaration this promotion rests on. Must be non-empty.

supersedes.description: Optional pointer to an earlier evaluation_id this record follows up on. Records are append-only: this never causes the earlier record to be removed or mutated.

corpus_role.description: AES-V2.17 / SUE-607, docs/architecture/LANGUAGE-QUALITY-ARCHITECTURE.md §7. discovery: traits may be derived from this reference. holdout: this reference validates a trait already derived elsewhere and must never have informed one. The assignment is made before trait extraction begins, never chosen afterwards to suit a result — a reference that has informed a trait can never be moved into holdout. Optional because not every reference feeds a language calibration.

language.description: The BCP-47-style language subtag this reference is evidence about, e.g. ko or ko-KR. Optional because a non-text reference (visual, audio, video) may not be about a language at all.

verdict.description: do_not_copy: the trait is admired but copying it would be imitation, not a transferable craft lesson.

applicability.description: What this evaluation is cheap to select for later. Ids are the profile-axis vocabularies in editorial/profiles/ — content_types, audiences, and surfaces each enumerate exactly the ids that axis holds. json-schema-lite cannot read the axis registry, so these enums are copies; scripts/test-schema-parity.mjs asserts they have not drifted from it. child-upper-elementary was added to the audience axis by SUE-570 and this copy was missed, which is the drift that guard now exists to catch.
